Thanks Alex — great questions. Quick summary up front: yes, we can pin Dedicated clusters to a single region (eu-west-1), and cross-region replication is optional and disabled by default. Our standard deletion flow provides an auditable wipe and attestation; timelines differ by artifact type (ephemeral caches vs. snapshots). I've attached a short runbook that outlines the steps and expected windows.

High-level answers:
- Region pinning: Dedicated tenants can be pinned to a single region. Control plane metadata remains in the private control plane you approve; customer data stays on nodes in the pinned region unless cross-region backup is enabled.
- Backups/snapshots: By default we keep backups in the same region. Cross-region replication is an optional add-on and only enabled with explicit customer consent.
- Deletion timeline & evidence: For application data and KV cache we mark data for deletion and remove live keys immediately; wipe jobs run within 48–72 hours and produce a job id + audit log. Block snapshots (cloud provider volumes) can take up to 7 days to be purged from provider-managed storage. We provide a signed deletion attestation and the audit log entries.

I'll loop in our ops team to confirm the exact SLA language we can include in Appendix B. Would you prefer the attestation as a signed PDF or a CSV export of the audit log?

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-erase-runbook.pdf (runbook summary)

Marissa / Rishi — confirming ops/security stance and proposed contract language. Short version below, feel free to copy into Appendix B.

Operational guarantees
- Region anchoring: Dedicated clusters can be configured to only provision compute and storage resources in the designated region (eu-west-1). Our provisioning templates will not create resources in other regions unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled by the customer in writing.
- Backups and snapshots: Default is same-region storage. Cross-region snapshot replication is a billable opt-in and requires customer approval.
- Deletion flow and evidence:
  1) Administrative request received -> data marked for deletion immediately.
  2) Live caches and KV entries are removed on the next safe checkpoint (typically within minutes).
  3) Wipe job scheduled within 48 hours; job performs zero-fill/secure delete procedures at the application layer and requests provider-level snapshot deletion.
  4) Provider snapshot purge can take up to 7 days depending on the cloud vendor; we track provider purge events and include that in the evidence.
  5) Deliverable: signed deletion attestation (PDF) plus audit log CSV lines that contain job id, timestamps, user id, and resource ids. We can commit to delivering the evidence within 5 business days of request (we've proposed 5 days operationally; legal can tighten/loosen).

Recommended contract text (copy-ready):
"Redwood will ensure that Customer data for the Dedicated deployment is stored in the Customer-designated region and will not be replicated outside that region unless Customer elects cross-region replication in writing. Upon Customer request for deletion, Redwood will execute the deletion workflow and provide a signed deletion attestation and audit log export within five (5) business days. Provider-level snapshot purges may take up to seven (7) calendar days; Redwood will include provider purge confirmations in the delivered evidence."

Attachments: deletion-evidence-template.csv (sample export format)

Hannah
